analog_blocks.name: pull
analog_blocks.evidence_paragraph:
* Medium: shielded twisted-pair copper cable (PROFIBUS cable type A).
  * Signaling: differential NRZ, half-duplex, balanced per EIA/RS-485.
  * Connector: 9-pin D-sub (DB9) or M12; pin 3 = B-line (RxD/TxD-P),
    pin 8 = A-line (RxD/TxD-N)

electrical_specs.raw: * Bus termination: 220 ohm pull termination network with 390 ohm

design_parameters.raw: * Character format (UART frame): 11 bits per character — 1 start bit,

signaling_summary: PROFIBUS-DP uses a balanced (differential) RS-485 two-wire line (A-line / B-line), half-duplex NRZ, with active 220 ohm termination at both segment ends (390 ohm pull-up to VP/+5 V and 390 ohm pull-down to DGND). The transceiver direction is switched per telegram (RTS). PROFIBUS-PA uses MBP / IEC 61158-2: a Manchester-encoded, bus-powered signal (current modulation +-9 mA around a DC base current) at 31.25 kbit/s, intrinsically safe.
modulation: DP: differential NRZ on RS-485 (A-line / B-line), half-duplex. PA: Manchester-encoded current modulation on the bus-powered MBP pair.
clocking: Asynchronous UART character timing on RS-485 (DP): 11-bit character (1 start + 8 data + 1 even parity + 1 stop), baud-rate-selected. PA: synchronous Manchester self-clocking at 31.25 kbit/s.

transmitter_specs_canonical.termination: 220 ohm with 390 ohm pull-up to +5 V (VP) and 390 ohm pull-down to DGND at both segment ends
transmitter_specs_canonical.character_format: 1 start + 8 data + 1 even parity + 1 stop (11 bits)
transmitter_specs_canonical.pa_phy: MBP / IEC 61158-2, Manchester, bus-powered, intrinsically safe

receiver_specs_canonical.fail_safe: active termination provides a defined idle level

cable_and_distance.cable: shielded twisted pair (PROFIBUS cable type A)
cable_and_distance.segment_length: up to 1200 m at 9.6-187.5 kbit/s; down to 100 m at 12 Mbit/s; repeaters extend the network
cable_and_distance.stations: up to 32 per segment without a repeater; up to 126 addressable per network with repeaters

encoding_role_in_analog: DP relies on standard RS-485 differential NRZ with an 11-bit UART character (even parity per character) and active bus termination for signal integrity; frame integrity comes from the 8-bit FCS checksum. PA uses Manchester encoding for self-clocking and DC balance on the bus-powered, intrinsically-safe MBP line.
